item.title: Energy-energy correlators in the large-charge limit of $\mathcal{N}=4$ super Yang-Mills theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.12414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the energy-energy correlator (EEC) in heavy states of four-dimensional $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang--Mills theory in the large-charge 't Hooft limit, in which the dimension $\Delta$ of the heavy operator (or, equivalently, its $R$-charge) is taken to infinity with the effective coupling $\lambda_Q \propto g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2\Delta$ held fixed. The relevant heavy-heavy-light-light four-point correlators are known to all orders in $\lambda_Q$ in this limit. For certain classes of operators, the perturbative series can be resummed to obtain exact finite-coupling expressions. We use these results to determine the corresponding EEC, whose dynamical part can be extracted from a double discontinuity of the four-point correlator. We determine the EEC at finite effective coupling and study its physical behavior as a function of $\lambda_Q$ and the angular separation between the detectors, both at generic angles and in the collinear and back-to-back limits.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Georgoudis, Max Jackson, Congkao Wen

item.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.26892v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the QFT-natural prescription in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem $\,$---$\,$ which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system $\,$---$\,$ is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Saurya Das, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: Nonlinear Response of Schwarzschild Black Holes at Arbitrary Perturbative Order
item.description: arXiv:2610.27048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish recursive integration-by-parts identities that symbolically reduce the inhomogeneous solutions of the Regge-Wheeler-Zerilli equation to a small set of master integrals, yielding the nonlinear response kernels of Schwarzschild black holes at arbitrary perturbative order. We further derive a closed ODE system that enables rapid, accurate, and stable numerical evaluation of these master integrals. To demonstrate our result, we compute quadratic, cubic, and quartic quasinormal-mode coupling coefficients as special cases of the response kernels.
item.dc:creator: Jiaqi Chen, Yu-Cun Xie

item.title: Nambu-Goldstone Bosons and Quantum Fisher Information
item.description: arXiv:2610.27054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The quantum Fisher matrix and geometric tensor are powerful tools for quantifying the nature of quantum systems. Unfortunately, the formalism needed to compute these quantities is opaque and has limited the development of physical intuition for their behavior, even in the ground state. For quantum systems with continuous symmetries, we know the ground state can be understood in a model-independent and intuitive way from the correlation functions of conserved currents and charges. In this paper, we demonstrate an equivalence between the quantum Fisher matrix associated with the ground states of systems with continuous symmetries and the Nambu-Goldstone. bosons produced by broken generators. We will show that the information metric defined by the Fisher matrix is the same as the Zamolodchikov metric that defines the coset space of the system. Next we show that the Uhlmann curvature associated with multi-parameter estimation is the same as the charge density matrix that defines the difference between type-A and type-B Nambu-Goldstone bosons. We demonstrate these connections in several examples and discuss the generalization to finite temperature.
item.dc:creator: Eugene Chen, Daniel Green

item.title: The Electron-Recoil Response Tail and the LZ High-Energy Event Background
item.description: arXiv:2610.27105v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We reconstruct the continuum electron-recoil contribution to the LZ background expectation from the collaboration's released simulation configuration. The released model specifies a definite response tail, but the published calibration information supplies no bound on how far the physical tail may depart from it at the probabilities the expectation depends on. Distributions reproducing the executable model's mean, variance, and standardised skewness exactly, and its event-conditioned 10, 50, and 90\% \(N_e\) quantiles to about one per cent, differ in the relevant tail probability by more than five orders of magnitude. The ladder is short: a tail agreeing with that central characterisation to 0.14\% in the quantiles lifts the electron-recoil contribution out of the negligible range, and one agreeing to 0.47\% makes it comparable to the entire background quoted for the comparison region. We go on to identify the measurements that would settle it.
item.dc:creator: Triparno Bandyopadhyay, Rajarajeswari Ramasamy, Nishitha TP

item.title: Searching for Dense Perturbers in Cold Dark Matter Simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.27236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recently, several low-mass, dense perturbers have been inferred from astrophysical observations of gravitational lensing, stellar streams, and satellite galaxies. If interpreted as dark matter subhalos, their inner densities exceed the predictions of the standard cold dark matter (CDM) model. We systematically investigate this tension using a CDM-only zoom-in simulation of a Milky Way analog. We analyze more than 5000 subhalos with masses down to $10^6\,M_\odot$ and reconstruct their inner density profiles using a tidal truncation model. The simulated subhalos are then compared with the observed compact perturbers in terms of their density profiles, enclosed masses, concentrations, and projected cylindrical masses. None of the simulated CDM subhalos is sufficiently dense to reproduce the inferred mass distributions of the observed perturbers. We further examine the redshift evolution of subhalo concentrations and derive a fitting function to characterize this evolution. Our findings motivate further investigations into exceptionally rare formation histories that could produce such dense perturbers, as well as the possibility of physics beyond the standard CDM model.
item.dc:creator: Xingyu Zhang, Hai-Bo Yu, Demao Kong, Ethan O. Nadler

item.title: Pretraining on boosted boson decays for polarization tagging of hadronic $W$ bosons
item.description: arXiv:2610.27346v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Longitudinally polarized weak bosons probe the unitarization of vector-boson scattering. At large boosts, longitudinal and transverse $W$ bosons produce jets with the same mass and two-prong structure, distinguished only by the decay angle. Longitudinal bosons are rare: they occur in only 0.3% of $W$+jet events at these large boosts. We ask where the polarization information of a boosted $W$ boson lies and how much a tagger can recover. Requiring both decay quarks within the jet truncates the decay-angle distribution at an edge set by $m/(p_T R)$, which we show bounds any hadronic polarization tagger. Within this acceptance, the decay angle carries essentially all the polarization information of a jet in $W$+jet events. Polarized samples are costly to simulate for vector-boson scattering, so we pretrain a point-edge transformer on $10^7$ unpolarized jets of boosted bosons, top quarks and QCD and test how much it recovers from few labels. Fine-tuned on 783 labeled jets per class with its transformer blocks kept fixed, the network pretrained to classify these jets improves on training from scratch, but generic pretraining on a broad mix of jets and a boosted decision tree on substructure observables do as well. The best taggers recover most, but not all, of the separation the decay angle allows, and student networks with a few hundred times fewer parameters, trained by knowledge distillation, match their teacher. More information lies outside the jet. The production angle, reconstructed with the recoiling jet, improves every tagger. In diboson production and vector-boson scattering at matrix-element level, the production kinematics carry more information than the decay angles of both bosons. Trading the generality of a jet tagger for an event-level tagger trained on the process thus brings significant gains, which measurements of longitudinal vector-boson scattering could exploit.
item.dc:creator: Saptaparna Bhattacharya

item.title: Parameter dependence of the mapping of the mean-field Ising model onto QCD in the first-order phase transition regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.27748v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We map the mean-field Ising equation of state onto the QCD phase diagram and investigate how scaling parameters alter the metastable and unstable regions, as well as the symmetrized pressure and density along an isotherm on the QCD $T-\mu_B$ phase plane. We find that, for both the conventional mapping scheme and the scheme valid in the small-quark-mass limit, increasing the scaling parameters $w$ and $\rho$ narrows the metastable and unstable regions. In the small-quark-mass-limit scheme, larger $w$ and $\rho$ reduce both the Ising-symmetrized pressure and density. For the conventional scheme, increasing $w$ reduces these quantities, while increasing $\rho$ raises the Ising-symmetrized pressure and has only a small effect on the density.
item.dc:creator: Xue Pan, Yuepeng Li

item.title: Constraints on Dark Matter Annihilation from Starlight-Induced Inverse Compton Emission in Omega Centauri
item.description: arXiv:2610.28068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The search for the particle identity of dark matter (DM) remains one of the foremost challenges in modern physics. In this work, we derive new constraints on the DM annihilation cross section $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ by considering the inverse Compton (IC) scattering of DM annihilation injected $e^+e^-$ off the starlight radiation field in Omega Centauri. As a likely remnant core of a dwarf galaxy, Omega Centauri provides a dense stellar environment that enhances the predict IC signal. Using multi-wavelength observations from Chandra and Fermi-LAT, we establish upper limits on $\langle\sigma v\rangle$ over a wide DM mass range from MeV to TeV. Notably, in the tens-of-MeV range, our results surpass existing constraints by approximately two orders of magnitude, exceeding $\langle\sigma v\rangle \sim 10^{-31}~{\rm cm^3\,s^{-1}}$. At several GeV to the TeV DM masses range, our constraints also remain stronger than existing limits. Our results demonstrate that starlight induced IC emission is an important component for indirect DM searches in dense stellar systems, establishing Omega Centauri as a powerful probe of the nature of DM.
item.dc:creator: Guan-Sen Wang, Xu Pan, Lei Feng

item.title: Hybrid Stars with Different Amount of Quark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.28408v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In a previous work, we explored the possibility of neutron stars with large quark cores. Through Bayesian inference, we obtained large sets of equations of state imposing constraints regarding the properties of nuclear matter, mass-radius data from NICER, the GW170817 data from Virgo-LIGO collaboration, perturbative QCD and causality. We also imposed that the maximum mass neutron star (NS$\text{max}$) must have a large quark core. In this work, we obtain a new set of equations of state (SmallQ set) with the same constraints as before. However, we relaxed the last constraint, imposing only that NS$\text{max}$ must have quark core, regardless of its size. We compare the results with the set from our previous paper constrained by NICER and GW170817 observations NJL-GW. For both sets, we use the Relativistic Mean Field model with nonlinear meson interactions for the hadron phase and the Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model with four- and eight-quark interaction terms for the quark phase. The SmallQ set has higher values of phase transition density, with 3 -- 4.5 $\rho_0$, compared to the NJL-GW, with 2 -- 2.5 $\rho_0$. The new set describes NSs with smaller radius and smaller tidal deformability, and is more compatible with NICER and GW170817 data. A difference in the quark matter composition is observed, with a larger quark strange fraction occurring in the SmallQ set. Within this set, $2 M_\odot$ NSs may contain little to no quark matter. It is shown that there is a non negligible fraction of EOS whose mass-radius curve presents a positive slope for 1.8 $M_\odot$ stars, while for nucleonic stars this fraction is negligible and for hyperonic stars the slope is always negative.
item.dc:creator: Milena Albino, Tuhin Malik, M\'arcio Ferreira, Constan\c{c}a Provid\^encia

item.title: High-Energy Evolution of Power-Suppressed Amplitudes
item.description: arXiv:2510.04914v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a new class of evolution equations which govern the high-energy behavior of power-suppressed scattering amplitudes. The equations can be viewed as a renormalization group flow with respect to the relevant effective field theory cutoff. A distinct feature of the method is in the use of a multidimensional cutoff to separate the relevant scales in problems characterized by a complex factorization structure. By adjusting the renormalization group variables to the geometry of the effective theory modes, our method naturally extends to a broad spectrum of physical problems including massive, massless, small, and wide angle scattering. We present applications to the benchmark processes of electron-positron forward annihilation and light quark mediated Higgs boson production/decays.
item.dc:creator: Maximilian Delto, Alexander Penin, Lorenzo Tancredi

item.title: Direct Detection of Leptophobic Dark Matter with Electronic Collective Excitations
item.description: arXiv:2510.18338v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Some new-generation dark matter detection experiments are primarily designed to search for the dark matter-electron interactions, but they can also be utilized to probe models in which dark matter couples exclusively to nucleon via the quantum effects. The hadronic loop-induced interactions can directly excite plasmons in semiconductors, thereby providing an additional channel for detecting the leptophobic dark matter. In this work, we investigate plasmon excitations in silicon detectors induced by boosted dark matter and cosmic-ray up-scattering dark matter via the hadronic loop process. By analyzing the available experimental data, we derive new exclusion limits on the leptophobic dark matter-nucleon scattering cross section in the sub-MeV mass range.
item.dc:creator: Yuanlin Gong, Yifan Hu, Ning Liu, Liangliang Su, Bin Zhu

item.title: New Bounds on Heavy QCD Axions from Big Bang Nucleosynthesis
item.description: arXiv:2510.23695v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) constraints on heavy QCD axions. BBN offers a powerful probe of new physics that modifies the neutron-to-proton ratio during the process, thanks to the precisely measured primordial Helium-4 abundance. A heavy QCD axion provides an attractive target for this probe, because not only is it a well-motivated hypothetical particle by the strong CP problem, but also it dominantly decays to hadrons if kinematically allowed. A range of its lifetime is thus excluded where the hadronic decays would significantly alter the neutron-to-proton ratio. We compute axion-induced modification of the neutron-to-proton ratio, and obtain robust upper bounds on the axion lifetimes, as low as 0.017 s for the axion mass higher than 300 MeV. Remarkably, this is stronger than projected future CMB bounds via $N_{\rm eff}$. Our bounds are largely insensitive to uncertainties in hadronic cross sections and the axion's branching fractions into various hadrons, as well as to the precise value of the initial axion abundance. We also incorporate, for the first time, several key improvements, such as scattering processes by energetic $K_L$ and secondary hadrons, that can also be important for studying general hadronic injections during BBN, not limited to those from axion decays.
item.dc:creator: Tae Hyun Jung, Takemichi Okui, Kohsaku Tobioka, Jiabao Wang

item.title: New Face of Standard Model: Neutral Magnetic Monopole
item.description: arXiv:2511.21174v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the standard model has a totally new type of monopole which has the neutral magnetic charge $4\pi/\be$, where $\be$ is the neutral charge. This tells that the standard model has two types of monopoles, the well known Cho-Maison type which has the magnetic charge $4\pi/e$ and the neutral type which has the neutral magnetic charge $4\pi/\be$. This necessitates the new neutral charge quantization rule $\be=4\pi n/\bar g$, in addition to the Dirac's electric charge quantization rule $e=4\pi n/g$. The mass of the new monopole could be less than the Cho-Maison monopole, around 3.28 TeV. We show how to construct the neutral monopole and clarify the topological origin of the new monopole. We discuss the implications of the new monopoles in physics.
item.dc:creator: Y. M. Cho

item.title: Models for differential cross section in neutron-proton scattering and their implications
item.description: arXiv:2512.02801v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A few analytic exponential models of the elastic differential cross section are proposed to analyse elastic neutron-proton (np) scattering. The models incorporate energy-dependent exponential slopes, power-law prefactors, and localized Gaussian modifications. Sub-leading exponential terms representing charge conjugation and isospin roles increase the applicability and quality of fit of the models to describe the differential cross section data of np, n \bar{p}, pp, and p \bar{p} elastic scattering. The models describe the characteristic features of all the elastic scattering data such as the dip-bump structure, shrinkage of the forward peak, and controlled curvature around the diffractive dip. Parameter values of the models are found by fitting the np experimental data in an energy range of (\sqrt{s}\) = 3.363 to 26.019 GeV and a momentum transfer range of 0.065 to 5.341 GeV^2. Employing the proposed models, total, elastic, and inelastic cross sections, slope parameters, interaction radii, and cross-section ratios for np scattering are calculated. A multi-stage error analysis is performed to evaluate the error in the calculations of the models. Implications of the results obtained by the models for nucleon structure and dynamics are discussed. The results show that the proposed models can be used for effective description of the np elastic differential cross section and for accurate estimation of the observables of elastic hadronic scattering. The findings of this study emphasize the significance of combining theoretical and phenomenological approaches, providing valuable information for investigations of future experimental data on the differential cross section from various colliders.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Saad Ashraf, Nosheen Akbar

item.title: Probing freeze-in dark matter using Bose-Einstein condensate in neutron star
item.description: arXiv:2605.22245v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neutron star (NS) is one of the most promising astrophysical targets to probe non-gravitational interaction of dark matter (DM) with visible matter. Their compactness makes them an ideal object which can capture particle DM efficiently over its lifetime using the DM-nucleon scattering cross-section. If DM particles are bosonic, then the captured DM population may form a Bose-Einstein condensate at the center of the NS, increasing the DM density significantly. In this work, we study the phenomenology of such scenario with enhanced DM annihilation rate due to the increased density in a condensate. The enhanced DM annihilation makes the NS surface `hotter' than in the standard cooling scenario. We show that the annihilation rate is enhanced by a factor of $\mathcal{O}(10^{15}-10^{20})$ if DM forms a condensate without large self-interaction, and DM with freeze-in value annihilation cross-section can heat up the NS to higher temperatures, bringing it within the reach of James Webb Space Telescope. It also allows us to probe DM-nucleon scattering cross section within the neutrino fog regime which will complement the terrestrial direct detection searches. Moreover, the enhanced annihilation from the condensate changes the lower limits on s-wave DM annihilation cross-section for capture-annihilation equilibrium and the formation of a black hole inside the NS. Finally, we show an example of a scalar DM model where such small annihilation and DM-nucleon scattering cross sections can generically arise.
item.dc:creator: Deep Ghosh, Anirban Das

item.title: $\lambda$, $\rho$, and $\sigma$ Regge trajectories for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ in the triquark-antitriquark picture
item.description: arXiv:2606.29380v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We propose Regge trajectory relations for the hexaquark ${(\bar{u}(cc))(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))}$ by using the Regge trajectory relations for diquarks and triquarks. With these newly derived relations, we investigate five series of hexaquark Regge trajectories: the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories. We demonstrate that, apart from the simplest $\lambda_1$-trajectories, the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories cannot be constructed by merely mimicking the meson Regge trajectories, since mesons possess no internal substructures. To derive these trajectories, one must account for the structure and internal substructure of hexaquark. Without this structural information, the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories could only be obtained through direct fits to available theoretical predictions or future experimental data. We demonstrate that the $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories for the hexaquark do not correspond respectively to the Regge trajectories for the triquark, antitriquark, diquark, and antidiquark. Nevertheless, their behaviors match those of the Regge trajectories for the triquark $(\bar{u}(cc))$, the antitriquark $(b(\bar{b}\bar{b}))$, the diquark $(cc)$, and the antidiquark $(\bar{b}\bar{b})$, in that respective order. Furthermore, we present rough mass estimates for the excited states corresponding to the $\lambda$-, $\rho_1$-, $\rho_2$-, $\sigma_1$-, and $\sigma_2$-trajectories.
item.dc:creator: Xin-Ru Liu, Qi Liu, Jiao-Kai Chen

item.title: Multiparameter Quantum Estimation and Degeneracy Structure in Three-Flavor Neutrino Oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2606.30222v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate three-flavor neutrino oscillations within the framework of quantum estimation theory using the quantum Fisher information matrix (QFIM). We analyze all six independent elements of the QFIM for the parameters $\theta_{23}$, $\delta_{\mathrm{CP}}$, and $\Delta m^2_{31}$, together with the corresponding quantum Cram\'er--Rao bounds and normalized parameter correlations. To connect the intrinsic quantum sensitivity of the neutrino state with experimentally accessible information, we further compare the QFI with the classical Fisher information (CFI) associated with flavor-probability measurements. We find that the difference between the quantum and classical information bounds is strongly dependent on the oscillation parameter and $L/E$, demonstrating that the efficiency with which the available quantum information is accessed depends on the measurement. We also investigate probability-degenerate solutions in the $(\theta_{23},\delta_{\mathrm{CP}})$ parameter space. Although different parameter sets can produce identical $\nu_\mu\rightarrow\nu_e$ appearance probabilities at specific $L/E$ values, their corresponding quantum states can remain distinct, as demonstrated by the quantum fidelity. The QFIM differences further reveal distinct local quantum-information geometries for these probability-degenerate solutions, while the corresponding CFIM differences show a parameter and $L/E$ dependent degree of distinguishability accessible through the flavor-probability measurement. Our results demonstrate that QFI and CFI provide complementary information for neutrino parameter estimation, with the QFIM serving as a measurement-independent quantum benchmark and the CFI characterizing the information accessible through a specified measurement.
item.dc:creator: Bhavna Yadav, Amir Subba, Yu Shi

item.title: Beyond Half-Life Limits: Robust Operator-Level Interpretation of Multi-Isotope Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decay
item.description:
arXiv:2607.04932v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Current and future neutrinoless double-beta decay ($0
u eta eta$) searches are usually characterized by half-life limits or projected sensitivities. For operator-level interpretation, however, the relevant question is not only the strength of the limit, but also the stability of the inferred constraints on low-energy lepton-number-violating (LNV) coefficients under changes of isotope and nuclear matrix-element (NME) method. Using $
u$DoBe, we convert half-life limits or projected sensitivities into limits on low-energy LNV coefficients for several choices of isotope, operator class, and NME method. We then compare the resulting limits across isotopes and NME methods. We quantify the stability by the spread of coefficient limits in non-observation scenarios and, for single-operator post-discovery benchmarks, by the spread of isotope-to-isotope half-life ratios. For the operator examples considered in this paper, the light-Majorana exchange mechanism gives the most stable interpretation. The selected dimension-six operators remain reasonably robust, while the short-range dimension-nine examples show a stronger dependence on isotope and NME-method choices. The same hierarchy appears in post-discovery benchmarks based on isotope-to-isotope half-life ratios: the reliability of such tests depends on whether the predicted half-life pattern remains stable across NME methods. A multi-isotope $0
u eta eta$ program therefore provides information beyond half-life reach by testing the stability of the operator interpretation. This spread-based analysis provides a practical way to identify which low-energy operator scenarios are suitable for isotope-ratio tests after a possible discovery, and which require more care before being connected to ultraviolet models of lepton-number violation.
item.dc:creator: K. Ishidoshiro

item.title: Multi-scale improved predictions for $\boldsymbol{pp \to t\bar{t}W^+ +X}$
item.dc:creator: Nikolaos Dimitrakopoulos, Malgorzata Worek

item.title: Inelastic Scattering Effects on Attenuation of Boosted Dark Matter
item.description: arXiv:2607.15098v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Earth attenuation is crucial for interpreting direct-detection constraints on boosted dark matter (DM), since scatterings with terrestrial nuclei can significantly modify the flux and energy spectrum reaching underground detectors. At boosted energies, inelastic nuclear channels beyond ordinary elastic scattering can become relevant, including quasi-elastic scattering, deep-inelastic scattering, and resonant scattering. In this work, we incorporate the resonant scattering of boosted dark matter (DM) off nuclei into the Earth-attenuation framework, in combination with the elastic, quasi-elastic, and deep-inelastic channels. We find that, in the heavy-mediator regime, resonant scattering can give a non-negligible contribution to the attenuation of boosted DM. Using the latest PandaX-4T data, we derive new constraints on the spin-independent boosted DM-nucleon cross section $\bar{\sigma}_n$.
item.dc:creator: Guanhua Gu, Liangliang Su, Lei Wu, Jin Min Yang

item.title: Laplace-Space Analysis of $xF_3$ Including Nuclear Effects and Gegenbauer-Polynomial Parton Distributions
item.description: arXiv:2607.28105v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a next-to-leading order (NLO) and next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD analysis of the non-singlet structure function $xF_3$, utilizing a Gegenbauer-polynomial representation for the input parton distribution functions (PDFs). The main objective is to assess how this flexible parameterization improves the extraction of valence quark distributions in the presence of nuclear effects. To this end, we incorporate nuclear modification factors into the input PDFs for heavy nuclear targets and solve the DGLAP evolution equations analytically in Laplace space. The structure function in Bjorken-$x$ space is then reconstructed using a Jacobi polynomial expansion. This combined framework enables a systematic investigation of the $xF_3$ data from the CCFR, NuTeV, and CHORUS experiments at both NLO and NNLO accuracies. We further examine the sensitivity of the extracted distributions to nuclear corrections and discuss their implications for the Gross--Llewellyn Smith, Bjorken, and Adler sum rules. Our results demonstrate that the Gegenbauer-polynomial PDF formalism provides a flexible and efficient framework for describing nuclear $xF_3$ data, yielding improved phenomenological consistency across a wide kinematic range.
item.dc:creator: Shahin Atashbar Tehrani (Rouhollah), Javad Sheibani (Rouhollah), Elham Astaraki (Rouhollah), Reyhaneh Farashaeian (Rouhollah), Kourosh (Rouhollah), Gheisari

item.title: Unfolding the low-energy reactor neutrino flux from CE$\nu$NS data with a finite Dirac sum
item.description: arXiv:2608.16107v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a novel method to analyze coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (CE$\nu$NS) data to extract the reactor antineutrino spectrum below the inverse beta decay threshold of 1.8 MeV, where it remains unmeasured. Adapting halo-independent analysis techniques developed for direct dark matter detection, we show how to obtain a best-fit and a pointwise confidence band for the integrated neutrino flux, without assuming a parametric form or smoothness prior for the spectrum. In our approach, which follows from convex geometry arguments, the differential neutrino rate is written as a linear combination of Dirac delta functions -- a finite Dirac sum (FDS) -- with a maximum number of terms determined by the number of data points. We apply our "FDS method" to mock CE$\nu$NS data for a low-threshold Ge detector and compare it with Tikhonov-regularized unfolding.
item.dc:creator: Muping Chen, Graciela Gelmini, Danny Marfatia, Koichiro Yasuda

item.title: Photon and gluon gravitational form factors of proton in QCD
item.description: arXiv:2608.23788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The energy momentum tensor allows us to probe the internal gravitational structure of the proton. The corresponding gravitational form factors contain information about its different contributions. In this work, we investigate the photon and gluon gravitational form factors of the proton within the QCD sum rule approach. Four independent gravitational form factors are computed in the range $0<Q^2<2\ \mathrm{GeV}^2$. The mass and scalar radii of the photon and gluon sectors are obtained in the forward limit. We find that the gluon mass radius is smaller than the photon mass radius. These results may be useful for future lattice QCD calculations and phenomenological studies.
item.dc:creator: Z. Asmaee, K. Azizi

item.title: Bose-Einstein condensation and dark radiation production from bosonic warm dark matter
item.description: arXiv:2608.29947v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the quantum statistical effects of bosonic warm dark matter (BWDM) in a microscopic model in which dark radiation (DR) is produced through the annihilation process $\chi\chi\rightarrow\phi\phi$ mediated by a Yukawa interaction. By decomposing the BWDM phase-space distribution into thermal and Bose--Einstein condensed components, we derive the thermally averaged annihilation cross sections for the thermal--thermal, thermal--condensate, and condensate--condensate channels, including the Sommerfeld enhancement. We find that, for the relatively small scalar DR masses considered here, the thermal--condensate channel remains subdominant. The transition between the thermal--thermal dominated and condensate--condensate dominated regimes is characterized by a critical condensate fraction $r_{\rm c}$, which depends mainly on the BWDM mass and the scalar DR mass. For condensate fractions above this critical value, the condensate--condensate channel can dominate the present-day annihilation rate. We further constrain the BWDM parameter space using the observational upper bound on the additional effective number of relativistic species, $\Delta N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.
item.dc:creator: Zhijian Zhang

item.title: Investigating three-body resonances in $\alpha\alpha\Omega/\Omega_{ccc}$ clusters within the $^{9}_{\Omega/\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ nucleus
item.description: arXiv:2609.00932v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the bound and resonant states of the $\alpha+\alpha+\Omega$ and $\alpha+\alpha+\Omega_{ccc}$ three-body systems, corresponding to $^{9}_{\Omega}{\mathrm{Be}}$ and $^{9}_{\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$, within the Gaussian expansion method combined with the complex scaling method. The $\alpha\Omega$ and $\alpha\Omega_{ccc}$ interactions are constructed by folding the $N\Omega$ and $N\Omega_{ccc}$ potentials obtained from lattice QCD calculations by the HAL QCD Collaboration with the nucleon density distribution of the $\alpha$ particle. The uncertainty associated with the $\alpha$-particle matter radius is also examined. For the $\Omega$ sector, the strong $N\Omega$ attraction generates deeply bound $0_1^+$, $2_1^+$, and $4_1^+$ states in $^{9}_{\Omega}{\mathrm{Be}}$, accompanied by a pronounced contraction of the $\alpha\alpha$ core, demonstrating a strong gluelike effect of the $\Omega$ baryon. An unconventional inversion between the $0_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ levels is also predicted. In contrast, the $\Omega_{ccc}$ baryon produces considerably weaker attraction: the $0_1^+$ state of $^{9}_{\Omega_{ccc}}{\mathrm{Be}}$ is weakly bound, whereas the $2_1^+$ and $4_1^+$ states remain resonances. Their resonance energies and widths exhibit a clear dependence on the strength of the $\alpha\Omega_{ccc}$ interaction. These results reveal qualitatively different gluelike behaviors of the $\Omega$ and $\Omega_{ccc}$ baryons and provide predictions for the spectroscopy of exotic multistrange and triply charmed hypernuclei.

item.title: Soft-Collinear Chiral Perturbation Theory for $B \to \pi$ form factors at large recoil
item.description: arXiv:2609.34696v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an effective hadronic theory for heavy-meson decays into energetic pions, organized by the approximate heavy-quark and chiral symmetries. The dynamical degrees of freedom of the theory consist of quasi-static heavy-meson fields coupled to soft and collinear pions, relevant for exclusive $B \to \pi$ transitions at large recoil energy ${E_\pi \simeq M_B/2}$. Our approach exploits the factorization of soft and collinear quarks in Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), leading to an emergent duplication of chiral symmetry in the two kinematic sectors. Promoting the soft and collinear chiral transformations to local symmetries enables us to systematically match non-local four-quark operators in SCET -- governing the soft-overlap contribution to heavy-to-light form factors -- onto effective operators constructed from hadronic fields below the scale of chiral symmetry breaking. As a first application, we compute the logarithmically enhanced pion-mass dependence of the $B \to \pi$ form factors at large recoil by calculating the one-loop matrix elements of the leading hadronic operators. We find that the non-local transition currents in our effective theory lead to a pattern of chiral-logarithmic corrections that is not compatible with the existing formulation provided by Hard-Pion Chiral Perturbation Theory.
item.dc:creator: Thorsten Feldmann, Jack Jenkins, Jaime del Palacio Lirola

item.title: Entropy Production and Thermalization in Heavy-Quark Langevin Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.22501v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Heavy quarks are often treated as Brownian probes of the quark-gluon plasma. We formulate the irreversible entropy balance of their momentum distribution and separate the production generated by collisions from the driving caused by an evolving medium. For linear dynamics the production splits into two positive contributions, from directed momentum and from the momentum width. A static bath obeys an exact H-theorem. A cooling bath adds an explicit driving term, and longitudinal Bjorken expansion enters as a separate kinematic drive rather than as collisional production. For a Bjorken temperature protocol we derive closed-form strong- and weak-coupling limits of the total production. At strong coupling it exceeds the initial relative entropy by a term linear in the relaxation time, whose quasistatic part has the thermodynamic-length form. At weak coupling it vanishes inversely with the relaxation time. A positive strong-coupling slope therefore guarantees maximal dissipation at intermediate coupling. The same structure holds for a relativistic Fokker-Planck equation with a J\"uttner stationary state, solved numerically for charm and bottom quarks under the temperature protocol. Linear-response coefficients computed from the static generator reproduce both limits, and the numerical entropy balance is satisfied to high accuracy.

item.title: Don't miss the forest for the trees: the Lyman alpha forest power spectrum in effective field theory
item.description: arXiv:2309.10133v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive an effective field theory (EFT) for cosmological Lyman alpha forest fluctuations valid for the power spectrum at the one-loop order. The ``bottom-up'' EFT expansion at the level of the transmitted flux is identical to the line-of-sight dependent bias model first derived by Desjacques et al. We confirm this result by a ``top-down'' derivation based on the exponential map of the optical depth field. Specifically, we show that the combination of the exponential map and conditions of renormalizability generates the same EFT expansion as the ``bottom-up'' approach. In passing, we point out inconsistencies of the tree-level perturbative expansion of the exponential map without counterterms. To facilitate practical applications, we generalize the FFTLog method for efficient calculations of one-loop integrals from new line-of-sight dependent operators. Finally, we compare the one-loop EFT model against data from the Sherwood hydrodynamic simulation. The theory fits the data with sub percent accuracy up to $k= $ 3 $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ at $z= 2.8$ for both 3D and 1D correlations. Our model can be readily used for cosmological full-shape analyses of Lyman alpha forest data.

item.title: Unveiling dark forces with measurements of the Large Scale Structure of the Universe
item.description: arXiv:2309.11496v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cosmology offers opportunities to test Dark Matter independently of its interactions with the Standard Model. We study the imprints of long-range forces acting solely in the dark sector on the distribution of galaxies, the so-called Large Scale Structure (LSS). We derive the strongest constraint on such forces from a combination of Planck and BOSS data. Along the way we consistently develop, for the first time, the Effective Field Theory of LSS in the presence of new dynamics in the dark sector. We forecast that future surveys will improve the current bound by an order of magnitude.

item.title: Nonflow Subtraction Beyond Two-Particle Correlations
item.description: arXiv:2606.10258v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Establishing collective flow in small collision systems is a crucial and necessary condition for pinning down the minimum conditions for quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formation. In two-particle correlations, nonflow has been subtracted with good control, pushing the reach of flow measurements down to very small event particle multiplicity $N$. However, the multi-particle nature of collectivity has not been established in the same $N$ regime, because the residual nonflow surviving the subevent procedure in multi-particle cumulants has never been quantified. We develop a general nonflow subtraction framework for $m$-particle cumulants, built around the approximate $1/N^{m-1}$ scaling of nonflow in the independent-source picture. Correlators containing $v_1$ serve as nonflow-dominated estimators, since the $p_{\mathrm T}$-integrated dipolar flow is expected to be small. Using HIJING as a controlled nonflow-only environment, we test the subtraction for three target observables ($\langle v_2^2\rangle$, $\langle v_2^2\delta p_{\mathrm T}\rangle$, and $c_2\{4\}$) in O+O at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 5.36$ TeV and 200 GeV and in $d$+Au at $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}} = 200$ GeV. Most of the nonflow is removed, with residual fractions typically within 20-30% when converted to the two-particle level, though the best estimator differs across the three targets. We identify a multiplicity-reweighting correction, previously overlooked in two-particle correlations, that explains the long-standing undersubtraction of the naive $1/N$-scaling method; its impact grows as a power of the correlator order. The framework gives a systematic route to nonflow subtraction beyond two-particle correlations, broadening the class of multi-particle observables accessible to the small-system flow program.
item.dc:creator: Zaining Wang, Jiangyong Jia, Jinhui Chen, Shengli Huang, Chunjian Zhang, Zhengxi Yan

item.title: Rapidity-even dipolar flow in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
item.description: arXiv:2607.17449v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Rapidity-even directed flow, $v_{1}^{\rm even}$, provides a sensitive probe of fluctuation-driven dipolar asymmetry in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, but its extraction is complicated by strong first-harmonic non-flow correlations, particularly those associated with global momentum conservation (GMC). In this study, $v_{1}^{\rm even}$ and its multi-particle correlations are investigated in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=200$\~GeV using the AMPT and HIJING models. An $\eta$-dependent weighting procedure is applied to suppress the leading GMC contribution. The GMC-suppressed HIJING results are strongly reduced for most $v_1$-related observables, while AMPT reproduces the characteristic sign-changing $p_T$ dependence of $v_{1}^{\rm even}$ and exhibits clear sensitivity to the partonic transport setting. The non-normalized mixed-harmonic correlations show a stronger transport dependence, whereas the normalized observables are substantially less sensitive to the absolute final-state response. Comparison with the initial-state eccentricity correlations shows that these normalized observables retain the underlying dipolar, elliptic, and triangular correlation structure after modification by the medium. These results demonstrate that GMC-suppressed rapidity-even dipolar flow correlations provide complementary constraints on initial-state fluctuations and their transformation during the final-state evolution.

item.title: Hamiltonian framework for Chiral Gauge Theories on a Disk Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.11035v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: I propose a Hamiltonian framework for chiral gauge theories (CGT) based on an existing Euclidean formulation, that uses 2n dimensional chiral fermions on the boundary of a 2n+1 dimensional disk. In the original Euclidean formulation, boundary gauge fields were extended into the bulk using $2n + 1$ dimensional gauge field equations of motion (EOM). This creates a bottleneck for constructing a Hamiltonian. I present an alternate proposal for extending the gauge fields into the bulk that is compatible with both a Hamiltonian framework and a Euclidean path integral. Applying this to Abelian gauge fields produces exact expressions of interior fields as a functional of the boundary fields, which can be directly used in a Hamiltonian formulation. Euclidean analysis of the new gauge field extension shows that it can preserve the non-perturbative content of the original construction, including the behavior of topological charge, associated chiral fermion zero modes and an absence of the strong CP problem when applied to the Standard Model. This construction opens up a route to a Hamiltonian treatment and future quantum simulation of CGTs on a disk boundary.
